title: How to Register and Fund your Mirror Trading International Account
description: A step by step guide to registering and funding your MTI account. Sign up today: ...

asr.full_text: How to register and fund your mirrortrading international account You will need the referral link of the person who invited you join mirrortrading international It will look something like this Click on that link and you will be taken to the registations screen Your sponsors user name will be displayed in the sponsor information section Next you will see auto placement is displayed Please check with your sponsor whether you should select the left or right-hand position. If you do not make a select you will automatically go into your sponsor's Team-Leg. Enter a user name and a password. Fill in your personal information, name, surname, email address, a valid Mobile No, and choose your country from the drop-down list. Read the Terms and Conditions, and then click I have read and accepted the Terms and Conditions. Once you have done this, click on the Register Button to complete the registration. A screen will come up with a confirmation message, which will confirm your login details. You will also receive an email from Mir that will confirm your log in details. You will also receive an email from Mirror Trading International confirming your registration. If you find this email in your spam folder you can inform your system that it is not spam and you'll be able to receive other emails from the company. Now that you have your login details please log-in to the back office at mymticlub.com then click on the Profile Button in the menu on the left. Please update your personal details and upload your proof of identity. Once you have done this, you can click the Update button. Adding funds to your Merit Trading International pool account. Click on the Wallet section on the left. A roll-down will appear. Click on the wallet section on the left. A roll-down will appear, click on add funds. The payment information screen will appear. You can either scan the QR code or carefully copy the Bitcoin address to your wallet. Make the payment by sending the Bitcoin, remember some wallets require you to verify the payment via email. Fill in the details The exact amount of Bitcoin you sent Enter the Blockchain Transaction ID . Upload the Proof of Payment screenshot, then click Submit. Once the admin has confirmed your Bitcoin transfer, it will appear in your trading account. In this case, your dashboard will confirm that you are a paid member. Each day you will receive a statement via email telling you the results of the trades. You can also log into your back office to see these results and your statements. Click on the view option to see your daily statement. That is your account and how to see the results from daily trading. Should you wish to refer your friends you can send them your registration link statement – that is your account and how to see the results from daily training. Should you wish to refer your friends, you can send them your registration link, or you can help them register, by clicking on the downline registration link. If you have questions or for more information please contact CLint.

textual.context: Presented as an instructional account-funding process with an admin-confirmation condition.
textual.potential_relevance: A requested Bitcoin transfer and proof-of-payment submission are explicitly tied to account funding, paid-member status, and access to reported trading results; this payment-to-benefit relationship may require later context assessment.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish any promised profit, guarantee, actual transaction outcome, legitimacy, or independent verification of the stated trading results; the QR code and Bitcoin address were not verified here.

textual.observation: Registration is tied to an inviter's referral link and sponsor/team placement, and the source later instructs members to refer friends or help them register.

textual.context: The records describe referral-based entry, sponsor placement, and onward referrals; whether this is promotion or discussion is unclear.
textual.potential_relevance: The relationship between entry through an inviter, placement in a sponsor's team leg, and instructions to bring in friends is an observable recruitment structure connected to account participation; later review may need to determine whether recruitment is a substantive condition of the offer.
textual.limitations: No commission, earnings amount, guarantee, or recruitment payout is stated, and the records do not independently establish how the team structure operates.

visual.observation: An MTI-branded signup screen shows "Sponsor Information" with a visible sponsor entry and placement selector, followed by fields for a username, password, first and last name, email address, mobile number, and country.
visual.context: Presented as part of a step-by-step account-registration demonstration; whether it is promotional or instructional is unclear.
visual.potential_relevance: The sponsor/placement step is coupled with collection of login credentials and direct contact details in the same registration workflow, creating a concrete onboarding-and-data-collection relationship that may merit review.
visual.limitations: The frames do not establish whether the sponsor field is required, how the information is used, or whether any money or benefit changes hands at this stage.

visual.observation: A branded back-office profile page requests a BTC address, date of birth, gender, an ID number, and an uploaded ID-proof file.
visual.context: The fields appear within an account-management interface associated with the same branded service.
visual.potential_relevance: The account workflow combines a digital-asset address with identity details and an ID-proof upload, a concrete sensitive-data-and-digital-asset handling relationship that may merit review.
visual.limitations: The frame does not establish whether the fields are mandatory, who receives the information, how it is stored, or whether any identity verification was completed.

visual.observation: A payment page displays a Bitcoin QR code and wallet address, asks for a Bitcoin amount, transaction ID/TxID, and proof-of-payment upload; a later frame shows an entered amount, transaction hash, and a Submit button.
visual.context: Presented as a funding or payment step within the account interface; the sampled frames do not show the final submission result.

visual.limitations: The frames cannot establish whether a transfer was completed, whether the displayed QR code or address was controlled by the service, or whether any promised outcome occurred.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it actively instructs viewers to join a Bitcoin-funded trading account through a sponsor referral, select a team position, and submit payment and proof of payment. It presents the account as a paid trading membership with daily trading results and bonuses, while also directing participants to recruit friends and use downline registration, tying participation to a multi-level team structure.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: S06 fits because the registration flow uses sponsors, left/right team placement, team-leg positioning, referrals, and downline registration, demonstrating a multi-person hierarchy connected to bonuses and participation. S03 is additionally supported because deposited Bitcoin is placed into a trading pool and the account displays trading results and trading bonuses.
